items.followUp: Define a saturated solution and identify its solute and solvent.

rubric.why: A solute is the substance that is dissolved in a solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the solute as the dissolved substance.

rubric.why: A solvent is the medium in which the solute dissolves.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the solvent as the dissolving medium.

modelAnswer: A solute is the substance that is dissolved in a solvent.
A solvent is the medium in which the solute dissolves.

items.followUp: What is an oxidizing agent? Give one example.

rubric.why: A reducing agent causes another substance to be reduced, for example by donating electrons.
rubric.description: Defines the action of a reducing agent.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a reducing agent reduces another substance, or for describing a valid reduction mechanism.

rubric.why: Hydrogen reduces copper oxide to copper in the stated example.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example of a reducing agent.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying hydrogen reducing copper oxide to copper, using names or formulas.

modelAnswer: A reducing agent is a substance that causes another substance to be reduced, for example by donating electrons.
Hydrogen is a reducing agent; it reduces copper oxide to copper: H₂ + CuO → Cu + H₂O.

items.followUp: Define valency and write the valency of chlorine.

rubric.why: Valency is an atom's combining capacity, related to the electrons it loses, gains, or shares.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for defining valency as an atom's combining capacity or in terms of electrons lost, gained, or shared.
Award 1 mark for stating that sodium (Na) has valency 1.

modelAnswer: Valency is the combining capacity of an atom, determined by the number of electrons it loses, gains, or shares.
